Homeschooling Is A Major Lifestyle Change
When you decide to homeschool, you will take on the duties and responsibilities of both a teacher and administrator. You will need to implement lessons, organize field trips, coordinate activities with other parents, and make sure you are compliant with state and local homeschool requirements. These responsibilities get added to your normal role as a parent. However, you cannot escape the fact that by dedicating more time to teaching in your children at home, your family may suffer a loss in income. The challenge is greater if you are a single parent. Careful budgeting and time management skills will be essential if you are going to homeschool.

Homeschooling Is Not An Accepted Form Of Education
Homeschooling has been around over one hundred years. In many ways, it predates our current public education system. Second, depending on the source you look at, the number of children homeschooling is estimated to be between 1.8 million and 2.5 million. Some of the fastest growth in homeschooling has been with minority families. Why? Put simply, every day parents see declining school budgets, poor academic ratings of schools, crime, bullying, and fewer resources. They want a change that will benefit their children, and homeschooling is well-established, with curriculum options and support groups.

Over these past few years, the concept of homeschooling has gained quite a lot of attention. Especially in a time like the COVID-19 pandemic, it has become an alternative to traditional schooling for many parents. The two texts express contrasting views on the debated homeschooling.

The author of the first text considers that homeschooling significantly alters one's way of life in the long run. When you choose to homeschool, you assume the roles and responsibilities of both a teacher and a head. Apparently, this involves delivering lessons, arranging excursions, coordinating activities with other parents, and ensuring compliance with state and local homeschooling regulations. These duties are in addition to your regular responsibilities as a parent. However, it is inevitable that homeschooling may lead to a reduction in your family's income. The challenge is even more significant for single parents; however effective budgeting and time management skills will be crucial if you plan to homeschool.

The author of the second text considers that homeschooling is not widely recognized as a legitimate form of education. Although, homeschooling has existed for over a century; what is more homeschooling existed before our current public education system. Minority families are experiencing some of the most rapid growth in homeschooling for parents observe decreasing school funding, low academic performance of schools, concerns about safety and bullying, and inadequate resources.

To conclude, I believe that homeschooling has both advantages and disadvantages. It is up to parents to make a thoughtful decision regarding homeschooling because each child varies in their educational needs and abilities.
